# Proposal: Guided AI GRC Build for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel and Sponsor
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, twelve weeks, US$60,000
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026 (with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg)

---

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. The Client's AI portfolio is at three stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

Three facts set the urgency. An internal audit finding from June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems. The Client has stated a target of "governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The Client also intends to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, although the start date is not fixed.

The regulatory drivers named are the EU AI Act and GDPR. Three constraints apply to this engagement:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

Whether the visual inspection system touches production staff is Unknown. That question is addressed in Week 4. Any conclusion on works council consultation duties should be confirmed with external counsel.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A consulting engagement would typically hand the Client a finished set of documents. A guided build works differently. The Client's own team builds the system each week, with workshop instruction and coaching alongside it.

This matters for Tamarack Instruments for three reasons:

1. **The audit finding stays with the Client.** It concerns a missing operating capability, not a missing document. Closing it credibly requires a team that can maintain the inventory after the program ends.
2. **ISO/IEC 42001 readiness depends on demonstrated operation.** It is shown through records generated over time. This program starts evidence collection in Week 8 so that operating records exist by Week 12.
3. **The program fits existing management systems.** The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. A team that builds the AIMS itself can judge where it should connect to those systems and where it should stand alone.

The program is grounded in three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. It works from two open frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Steering checkpoints draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Inventory sequence for Week 2:**

1. **Customer service chatbot first.** It is the only system the Client describes as deployed.
2. **Visual inspection pilot second.** It carries the stated Q2 2027 production objective.
3. **Sales forecasting third.** It enters as a planned entry so that it is governed from intake.

The inventory process also includes a discovery sweep for AI systems not named in the Profile Block. Their existence and number are Unknown.

**ISO/IEC 42001 themes.** The readiness themes in the table below indicate where each week's artifacts contribute to future ISO/IEC 42001 work. They are not a promise of certification or of any audit outcome.

**Integration with incumbent frameworks.** The Profile Block names the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 QMS. It does not state which registers, processes or records the Client holds within them. Integration points are therefore Unknown for every week until the Client confirms the specific artifact each AIMS element would attach to. Each week below lists the question the team will answer.

| Week | Focus, tailored to the Client | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point (ISMS / QMS) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles; confirm the build lead, the second governed workflow and steering composition | Context, leadership, roles | Unknown: confirm whether existing management system governance documents should host the AIMS charter |
| 2 | AI system inventory: chatbot, visual inspection pilot, sales forecasting, plus discovery sweep | Context, AI system scope | Unknown: confirm whether an asset register exists to link to |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology, including EU AI Act classification of each inventoried system (confirm with external counsel) | Planning, risk criteria | Unknown: confirm whether an ISMS risk methodology exists to align with |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments for the chatbot and visual inspection, including GDPR interplay, EU data residency and whether production staff are affected | Planning, AI system impact assessment | Unknown |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Planning, risk treatment | Unknown: confirm whether a risk register exists to integrate with |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Leadership, AI policy | Unknown: confirm the existing policy hierarchy |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance, with emphasis on the visual inspection path from pilot to production | Operation, lifecycle | Unknown: confirm whether QMS change or release procedures exist to connect to |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Operation, third parties; support, documented information | Unknown: confirm whether a supplier assessment process exists |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight using Slow AI Kitchen | Operation, human oversight | Unknown |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring, including inspection accuracy monitoring approach for the pilot | Performance evaluation | Unknown: confirm whether QMS measurement records exist to link to |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | Improvement, nonconformity | Unknown: confirm whether an ISMS incident process exists |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Performance evaluation, internal audit, management review | Unknown |

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS. At Week 12 it consists of six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Governed workflows.** The customer service chatbot is the only use case the Profile Block describes as deployed. The second governed workflow is therefore Unknown and is a Week 1 decision. The visual inspection system is described as piloting, so its production status during the program is Unknown. This proposal does not assume it will reach production within the twelve weeks.

**Evidence collection.** Collection begins in Week 8. This allows at least four weeks of operating records by Week 12.

Two points need confirmation before Week 1:

- **Build lead.** The program needs one named build lead to coordinate asynchronous work. That person is Unknown.
- **Internal auditor independence.** The two internal auditors will take part in the build. The Client should decide in Week 1 how to protect their independence for any future audit of the AIMS.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** confirms scope, team, delivery risks and the second governed workflow.
- **Week 6:** reviews spine status and blockers, and takes any scope decisions. This includes progress on the visual inspection lifecycle path.
- **Week 12:** reviews attestation against the six-element definition and approves a twelve-month operating plan.

Steering composition is Unknown and is confirmed in Week 1.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format.** All sessions are virtual. Each week includes one live workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions. Session times, time zones and the storage location for program artifacts and evidence are Unknown and are agreed in Week 1. They must be consistent with the constraint that customer data stays in the EU.

**Price.** The price is US$60,000. This is within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. The end date of the Client's fiscal year is Unknown, so the Client should confirm that the engagement falls within it. Invoicing terms are Unknown and will be set out in the engagement agreement (confirm with external counsel).

**Timing.** The program start date is Unknown, and so is the exact production date for visual inspection within Q2 2027. For the twelve weeks to close before Q2 2027 begins on 1 April 2027, the build would need to start no later than early January 2027.

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. To support it, we ask the Client to confirm the following:

2. The build lead.
3. The candidate second governed workflow.
4. Steering composition.
5. Which existing ISMS and QMS artifacts, if any, the AIMS should attach to.
